articles.title: A Big Map Shake-Up: Why Virginia's Vote Just Got Tossed Out
articles.summary: Imagine voting for something and then a court says it didn't count! That happened in Virginia, where 1.6 million people said yes to new voting maps. Now those maps are gone, and Republicans are redrawing lines across the South to win more seats.

articles.title: Redrawing the Map: How a Court Ruling Is Changing Who Wins Elections
articles.summary: A Supreme Court decision has set off a race to redraw voting maps in the South. In Tennessee, a new map could wipe out the only Democratic district. Republicans could gain 8 more seats, making it harder for Democrats to win back the House.

articles.title: Iran Says a Tiny Waterway Is as Powerful as an Atomic Bomb
articles.summary: Iran's leaders are talking up the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow sea passage where lots of the world's oil travels. One official said controlling it is like having an atomic bomb because it can shake the whole global economy. This comes as Iran and the U.S. try to make a deal.
